stem.en: A sewage plant runs in this order: sedimentation, coagulation, filtration. Why does it not start with the filter bed?

text.en: The filter bed costs the most, so the plant saves money by using it last.
The heavy solids would reach the sand first and block it, so the water would stop flowing.
Coagulant only works on water that has already passed through sand and gravel.
The order does not matter. Any order gives the same clean water, and the pipes decide it.

explanation.en: A filter bed holds back small bits, but a full load of heavy solids would block it. Sedimentation removes the heavy solids first, and coagulation makes the fine particles clump and sink. Then the bed has only a little left to catch. Cost is not the reason, and coagulant works on dirty water directly, as alum does in a jar.

hints.en: What would happen to the sand if all the heavy solids arrived at once?
